chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini who said: A group of our companions narrated linking it up to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Acquire knowledge, for learning it is a good deed, studying it is glorification (tasbih), searching for it is jihad, teaching it to one who does not know it is charity, and giving it to its people is a means of drawing near (to God), because it is the landmarks of the lawful and the unlawful, and its path leads to Paradise. It is a companion in loneliness, a guide in ease and hardship, a weapon against enemies, and an ornament among friends. God elevates people by it, making them leaders in goodness to be followed; their deeds are observed and their traces emulated. Angels desire their friendship, brushing them with their wings during their prayers. Everything, even the fish of the seas and their creatures, and the beasts of the land and their livestock, asks forgiveness for them, because knowledge is the life of the hearts, the light of the eyes from blindness, and the strength of the bodies from weakness. God places its bearers in the ranks of the best, granting them seats with the righteous in this world and the Hereafter. By knowledge, God is obeyed and worshipped; by knowledge, God is known and grasped; by knowledge, ties of kinship are connected; and by it, the lawful and unlawful are recognized. Knowledge is the leader of action, and action follows it. God inspires it to the blessed and deprives the wretched of it.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and social virtues of seeking knowledge in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a comprehensive theological framework where knowledge is not merely intellectual but an ontological state that animates the soul and dictates moral action. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the learned as spiritual leaders whose piety commands the respect of angels and all creation, reinforcing the concept of 'ilm as the prerequisite for righteous practice (amal).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 20-12 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtayni who narrated a group of friends who linked it up to the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali(MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“Acquire knowledge since learning is a good deed, teaching equals saying God’s glorifications, and discussing about knowledge equals participating in a holy war. Teaching knowledge to the one who doesn’t know it is giving charity. Granting knowledge to the proper persons brings God’s pleasure, since one knows the lawful and the unlawful using knowledge and knowledge would lead its seeker to Paradise. Knowledge is a guide in case of fear; it is a companion in case of loneliness; it is a guide in case of hardships; it is a weapon against the enemies; and an ornament in the presence of friends. God promotes some people by means of knowledge to such a high rank that they are the leaders of goodness and must be obeyed. Their deeds must be taken into consideration and their works must be followed. The angels are inclined to be their friends and they anoint them with their own wings while they pray. Everything including the fish in the sea, the beasts in the desert and the quadrupeds ask for forgiveness for them since knowledge brings life to the hearts and light to the eyes and power against sluggishness. God opens the doors to the homes of the good people for the learned men. He grants them association with the good ones in this world and in the Hereafter. God is obeyed and served by means of knowledge. God is recognized as One by means of knowledge. The bonds of relationship are fastened by means of knowledge. What is lawful and unlawful is recognized by means of knowledge. Knowledge is the prelude to action. Any action follows knowledge. God inspires it to the blessed ones and deprives the miserable ones from it.’
